original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

scope_change_reason: The assigned block-decoder route is crowded by open P112 masked-decoder work. This package isolates a different exact support-change mechanism: independent rational null-dependency gauges on at most two orthogonal blocks of the merged coordinate-frame-plus-root P112 decoder, with every exterior row fixed to its canonical sparsest gauge. It supplies an exact monotone exterior-rank lower bound rather than repeating Cycle 15's shared ternary shift search.
actual_scope: For the coordinate-frame-plus-root nine-normal decoder on the fixed P112 puncture, partition the 112 live E8 lines by the stated increasing-index greedy rule into 14 disjoint orthogonal eight-line blocks. For each of the 14 blocks and 91 unordered block pairs, vary arbitrary rational coefficient gauges only on the selected block union and pin every exterior row to Frame.sparsest(i). Compute the exact F2 copied-information rank of the exterior rows as a lower bound for every completion.
bottleneck_link: A decoder with copied-information cost below 64 could improve the P112 local invoice before frame and realization charges. The exact exterior-row relaxation floors this entire one/two-block family at 64 or more, so no favorable completed budget exists in this scope.
stop_rule: Compute the exact exterior-row rank floor for all 14 singleton blocks and all 91 block pairs. Stop if every floor is at least the existing cost 64; do not extend to three blocks, different gauges outside the selected union, another frame or another puncture.
evidence: The exact census gives one-block floors 67 twice and 68 twelve times; pair floors 64 once, 67 twenty-four times and 68 sixty-six times. The coordinate-root baseline costs 68 and is exact on all 112^2 live pairs. Three arbitrary rational dependency-gauge completions pass the exact identity; a coefficient mutation fails. No floor is a new decoder cost or kappa.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, exact enumeration, proof checks and writing. No independent human review or proof-assistant formalization is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can coordinated gauge changes on three or more blocks lower the exterior-row floor below 64?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the next size of local support change that could leave copy-cost headroom.
open_questions.first_step: Compute exact fixed-exterior ranks for all three-block unions before enumerating any gauge choices.
open_questions.blocked_by: No three-block floor has been computed; the current result is intentionally limited to one or two blocks.

open_questions.question: Can a different nine-normal frame on this puncture make one- or two-block edits favorable?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That would change the fixed-frame restriction behind this local obstruction.
